{{short description|Subalgebra of E8 containing E7}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:E<sub>7½</sub>}}
In [[mathematics]], the [[Lie algebra]] '''E<sub>7½</sub>''' is a subalgebra of [[E8 (mathematics)|E<sub>8</sub>]] containing [[E7 (mathematics)|E<sub>7</sub>]] defined by Landsberg and  Manivel in order
to fill the "hole" in a dimension formula for the [[En (Lie algebra)|exceptional series E<sub>''n''</sub>]] of simple Lie algebras. This hole was observed by [[Predrag Cvitanović|Cvitanovic]], [[Deligne]], Cohen and de Man. E<sub>7½</sub> has dimension 190, and is not simple: as a representation of its subalgebra E<sub>7</sub>, it splits as {{nowrap|E<sub>7</sub> ⊕ (56) ⊕ '''R'''}}, where (56) is the 56-dimensional [[irreducible representation]] of E<sub>7</sub>. This representation has an invariant [[Symplectic vector space|symplectic form]], and this symplectic form equips {{nowrap|(56) ⊕ '''R'''}} with the structure of a [[Heisenberg algebra]]; this Heisenberg algebra is the [[Nilradical of a Lie algebra|nilradical]] in E<sub>7½</sub>.
